newsitem.title: GREECE: Hard drachma policy to be tested - Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: Hard drachma policy to be tested - Deutsche.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the hard drachma policy was likely to continue for some time but prospective ERM membership, persisting external imbalances and an overvalued currency pointed to problems ahead.

"The policy of a 'hard drachma', which aims to keep the exchange rate versus the ecu stable this year, will likely be continued successfully for some time thanks to the progress made with stabilisation," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in its April report.

But Greek ambitions to join EMU in 2001 at the latest coupled with an overvalued drachma on the basis of PPP and persisting external imbalances means that parities would have to be realigned in order to be sustainable, it said.

"..the exchange rate upon entry would be below the current market level. This could be reflected in exchange-rate expectations next year," it said. "We see this as a downward risk to our 12-month drachma/ecu forecast."
The drachma would have to be a member of the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) two years prior to Greece's entry into EMU, it added.
The majority of Greek bankers polled recently by Reuters predicted that the drachma would enter the ERM in the spring of 1999.
Greece's current account deficit widened to $4.5 billion in 1996 from $2.85 billion in 1995 but economists have pointed out that it is still manageable standing at 3.8 percent of GDP.
The drachma slid 1.0 percent against the ecu in 1996 versus 3.0 percent in 1995, conforming to the pre-announced foreign exchange policy of the Bank of Greece.

The central bank has said that its 1997 foreign exchange policy would retain its anti-inflationary character and the stability of the drachma against the currencies that make up the ecu would be a basic goal of monetary policy.
Bank of Greece aims at bringing consumer price inflation down to 4.5 percent at year-end and below 3.0 percent by end-1998 from 6.0 percent currently.

But Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said an estimated 8.0 percent growth in unit labour costs this year was incompatible with sustained improvement in inflation and forecast inflation settling between 5.5 and 6.0 percent at end-1997.
The national economy ministry said it targeted CPI-based inflation to end the year at 4.5 percent and revised it upwards later to 5.0 percent.
"The downward trend in inflation will likely continue over the next few months but could falter in the later part of the year," it added.

Fiscal balances will improve in 1997 on rapidly falling interest rates on Greece's public debt but the general government budget deficit will probably be 5.5 percent of GDP, much higher than the government's 4.2 percent of GDP target on sluggish revenues. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
